sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Pneumonia is an acute infection of the lung parenchyma (alveoli and lower respiratory tract) leading to inflammatory exudate and consolidation. It is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, often categorized by the environment of acquisition (CAP, HAP, VAP) to guide empiric antimicrobial therapy.

rows: P. aeruginosa, S. aureus (MRSA), Klebsiella, E. coli

content.explanation: C: Confusion (new onset); U: Urea >7 mmol/L (20 mg/dL); R: RR ≥30/min; B: BP (SBP <90 or DBP ≤60); 65: Age ≥65 years. (0-1: Home; 2: Inpatient; 3+: ICU/Stepdown)

sections.title: Emergency Red Flags
content: Septic Shock requiring vasopressors
Acute Respiratory Failure (PaO2/FiO2 ratio <250)
Multilobar opacities on CXR
Leukopenia (WBC <4,000) or Thrombocytopenia (<100k)
Hypothermia (Core temp <36°C)
New onset uremia (BUN >20)

branches: Symptoms: Productive cough (rusty/green sputum), Pleuritic chest pain, Rigors, Dyspnea
Physical Signs: Bronchial breath sounds, Dullness to percussion, Increased tactile fremitus
Auscultation: Crackles/Rales, Egophony ('E' to 'A'), Whispered pectoriloquy
Atypical: Dry cough, Diarrhea (Legionella), Ear pain (Mycoplasma/Bullous Myringitis)

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Pathway
content: Step 1: Imaging — PA/Lateral CXR (Gold Standard: look for air bronchograms/infiltrates). Consider CT for occult cases.
Step 2: Labs — CBC (Leukocytosis with left shift), BMP (Uremia, Hyponatremia in Legionella), Procalcitonin/CRP.
Step 3: Microbiology — Sputum Gram stain/Culture, Blood Cultures x2 (if severe), Legionella/S. pneumo Urinary Antigens.
Step 4: ABG/VBG — Assess for hypoxemia, hypercapnia, or acid-base derangements in distressed patients.
Step 5: Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) — Look for 'Shred Sign', B-lines, and pleural effusions.

rows: Bilateral opacities, Kerley B lines, Cardiomegaly, high BNP, responds to diuretics.
Pleuritic pain, clear CXR (usually), Wedge-shaped infarct (Hampton's Hump), high D-Dimer/CTPA positive.
Cough without focal consolidation on CXR, usually viral.
Chronic weight loss, non-resolving infiltrate, hilar lymphadenopathy.

sections.title: Empiric Management: CAP (Outpatient)
content: Healthy (No Comorbidities): Amoxicillin 1g TID OR Doxycycline 100mg BID.
With Comorbidities (DM, CKD, COPD): Augmentin + Macrolide (Azithromycin 500mg) OR Respiratory Fluoroquinolone (Levofloxacin 750mg).
Duration: 5-7 days based on clinical stability.

sections.title: Inpatient/ICU Management Protocols
content: Standard Inpatient: Ceftriaxone 1-2g IV QD + Azithromycin 500mg IV/PO.
ICU Coverage: Ceftriaxone + Levofloxacin (Double coverage for Legionella/Pneumo).
MRSA Concern: Add Vancomycin (trough 15-20) or Linezolid 600mg BID.
Pseudomonas Concern: Piperacillin-Tazobactam 4.5g q6h or Cefepime 2g q8h.

branches: Pulmonary: Parapneumonic effusion, Empyema (pH <7.2), Lung Abscess, Necrotizing pneumonia
Systemic: Sepsis/SIRS, Septic Shock, ARDS, Multi-organ failure
Cardiac: Increased risk of MACE (Major Adverse Cardiac Events) for 1 year post-infection

sections.title: Landmark Studies & Recent Advances
content: CAPE COD Trial (2023): Hydrocortisone therapy reduced 28-day mortality in patients with severe CAP.
MRSA Nasal PCR: High negative predictive value (~98%); useful for de-escalating anti-MRSA therapy in HAP/VAP.
Procalcitonin-Guided Therapy: Useful for antibiotic cessation in clinically stable patients, but should not delay initiation in the ED.
Pneumococcal Vaccine (PCV20/Vaxneuvance): Shift toward higher-valent conjugate vaccines for adult prophylaxis.

content.explanation: P: Pleural effusion >1cm on lateral decubitus needs thoracentesis; E: Elderly patients may lack fever (present with falls/delirium); A: Aspiration risk is highest in posterior segments of upper lobes/superior segments of lower lobes; R: Repeat CXR in 6-8 weeks for smokers >40 to rule out underlying malignancy; L: Legionella often causes hyponatremia and high LFTs; S: S. aureus pneumonia often follows an influenza infection.

sections.title: Surgical/Procedural Interventions
content: Thoracentesis: Indicated for any significant parapneumonic effusion.
Chest Tube (Tube Thoracostomy): For empyema, loculated fluid, or pH < 7.2.
VATS (Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery): For decortication in complex/chronic empyema.
Bronchoscopy: Useful in non-resolving pneumonia or for BAL in the immunocompromised.

sections.title: Special Populations: Pediatrics
content: Neonates (<3 weeks): Group B Strep, E. coli, Listeria. Rx: Amp/Gent.
Infants (3w-3m): C. trachomatis (staccato cough).
Children (Preschool): Viral (RSV) is most common.
Atypical Pathogens: Mycoplasma is more common in children >5 years.
